## Summary

TraceLens perf reports compare each op's measured time with a roofline. This PR lets you add your own op projection from an `--extension_file`, with no change to TraceLens. An op projection reads an op's work (its category, parameters, FLOPs, and bytes) and returns values to report, usually a predicted time but also anything else per op, such as the kernel configuration a library would pick. Its values show up as columns in every perf sheet.

```python
# my_extension.py
def my_gemm_projection(work, arch):
    if work.category != "GEMM":
        return None                                   # not covered
    p = work.params
    return {"time_us": predict(p["M"], p["N"], p["K"]),
            "Tile": "256x128x64"}                     # extra columns are optional

op_projections = {"MyModel": my_gemm_projection}
```

```bash
TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch --profile_json_path trace.json.gz \
  --gpu_arch_json_path mi300x.json --extension_file my_extension.py
```

This adds `MyModel Time (µs)`, `MyModel TFLOPS/s`, `MyModel TB/s`, `MyModel Tile`, and `Pct MyModel` (the prediction as a percentage of the measured time) to the per-op sheets and the summaries.

## How it works

- A *perf model* describes an op's work: shapes, FLOPs, bytes. An *op projection* turns that work into per-op values: a time, extra columns, or both.
- `compute_perf_metrics` now measures the op, describes its work once as an `OpWork`, and runs every registered op projection through one loop and one column writer.
- Every op projection has the same interface: `fn(work, arch)` returns a dict or `None`. `time_us` fills the time, TFLOPS/s, TB/s, and Pct columns; every other key becomes a `<label> <key>` column. If one raises or returns anything else, its columns stay empty for that op and TraceLens warns once; the rest of the report is unaffected.
- `OpWork` carries `category` (backward ops get the backward category), a copy of `params` (the report's `param:` columns), `gflops`, `bytes_moved`, `compute_spec`, `bwd`, and the `perf_model` itself. Every op projection gets the whole `OpWork` and uses whatever it needs: Origami reads the GEMM parameters, and the roofline reads FLOPs and bytes.
- Roofline and Origami are op projections too, written the same way, so built-in and external ones produce the same columns. Summary sheets find labels from the columns, so a new op projection needs no report code.
- From Python: `analyzer.register_op_projection(label, fn)`.
- Kernel filters (`kernel_filters = {"label": fn}`) report an op's throughput over a subset of its kernels. They replace the hardcoded non-data-movement option.

Built-in op projections:

| Label | Enabled by | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `Roofline` | a GPU arch | every op with a perf model |
| `Origami` | `--enable-origami-gemm` | GEMMs |
| `SDPA Tile Origami` | `--enable-origami-sdpa-tile` | attention, forward and backward |

The SDPA tile model splits attention into one Q·Kᵀ and one P·V tile GEMM on one CU, timed by Origami, and adds softmax and memory terms. `sdpa_tile_time_us` takes a `gemm_time` callable, so another GEMM model can reuse the tiling.

Docs: "Add an op projection" in the PyTorch report how-to, op-projection columns in the column reference, and a stub in `examples/external_op_projection_stub.py`.

## Behavior changes

- `--enable-origami` is now `--enable-origami-gemm`, and the Python keyword `enable_origami` is now `enable_origami_gemm`. There's no alias.
- Attention times moved out of the `Origami` columns, behind `--enable-origami-sdpa-tile` with their own `SDPA Tile Origami` columns. With real Origami they're now filled: one-CU tiles used to fail Origami's architecture lookup, so no time was produced.
- The external GEMM simulator backend and `GEMM_SIMULATOR_PATH` are removed, and so is `python_path`, which only chose that simulator's interpreter: the `--python_path` flag, the `TreePerfAnalyzer` and report-generator keyword, and the perf model constructor argument. Perf models that subclass a built-in one and pass `python_path` to `super().__init__` should drop it.
- `TraceLens/PerfModel/run_perf_model.py` is removed. The Origami how-to shows the equivalent Python call.
- `GEMM.get_simulation_time_func` is replaced by `TraceLens.PerfModel.origami_helper.gemm_time_us`, which also owns the Origami dtype map. `simulation_dtype_map` is removed.
- Perf models no longer take `enable_origami`. The SDPA tile model moved out of the `SDPA` class into `TraceLens/PerfModel/sdpa_tile.py` (`sdpa_tile_time_us`, `sdpa_fwd_time_us`, `sdpa_bwd_time_us`), unchanged. It times its tiles with the `gemm_time` it's given, and the `SDPA Tile Origami` op projection passes Origami's. `SDPA.get_simulation_time*` and `SDPA.tile_gemm_time` are removed.
- The `non_data_mov` argument of `compute_perf_metrics` is replaced by kernel filters; `examples/kernel_filter_example.py` reproduces the old `Non-Data-Mov` columns.
- In summary sheets, Origami `TB/s` is aggregated once per shape, like its time.
- JAX reports gain roofline columns when an arch is given.

GEMM Origami values are otherwise unchanged from `main`.

## Not in this PR

- Numeric fixes to the attention tile model, such as backward tiling and choosing flash tiling by `flash_impl` instead of by class name. These change numbers, so they'll come separately with a before/after comparison.
- Six common attention ops are missing a dtype, so they get no roofline or Origami columns: #1099.

## Testing

- `tests/test_op_projections.py` and `tests/test_external_op_projection.py` cover the `(work, arch)` interface, the column writer, error isolation (including return values other than a dict or `None`), extension loading, kernel filters, and end-to-end reports. `tests/test_origami_reference.py` pins real Origami GEMM and SDPA tile times on a bundled trace.
- CI's unit test command (`-m "not gpu"`) on Linux with real `rocm-origami`: 3689 passed, 46 skipped. The one other failure was the pytest 9.2 break fixed on `main` in #1167, which this branch now includes.
- Every report sheet (8 bundled traces × 8 configurations, 696 CSVs) was compared commit by commit. Every difference is one of the behavior changes above. The final rename to op projections and the move to `(work, arch)` change no values; the perf-report regression tests pass against their reference CSVs.

+"""Op projections: per-op predictions computed from an op's work.
+
+A *perf model* (:mod:`TraceLens.PerfModel.perf_model`) says what work an op
+does: its shapes, FLOPs and bytes. An *op projection* takes that work and
+returns what to report for the op, usually a predicted time but also values
+such as a kernel configuration. :class:`TreePerfAnalyzer` measures an op,
+describes its work as an :class:`OpWork`, and runs every registered op
+projection on it::
+
+    def op_projection(work, arch):
+        if work.category != "GEMM":
+            return None
+        return {"time_us": time_us, "Tile": "256x128x64"}
+
+``work.category`` is the perf-model class's ``category`` (``"GEMM"``,
+``"SDPA_fwd"``, ...), or its ``bwd_category`` (``"SDPA_bwd"``, ...) for a
+backward op, which is ``None`` for ops without one (GEMM). ``work.params`` is
+a copy of the perf model's ``param_details``, the same values as the
+report's ``param:`` columns; any key may be missing (for example
+``transpose``, which is only set when the kernel name parses). ``arch`` is
+the GPU arch dict of the report, or ``None``.
+
+The output is ``None`` (no projection for this op) or a dict. ``time_us`` is
+optional; every other key ``name`` becomes a ``<label> <name>`` column, and
+only scalar values (numbers, strings, bools) are written. With a time, the
+label also gets ``<label> Time (µs)``, ``<label> TFLOPS/s``, ``<label> TB/s``
+and ``Pct <label>`` (time as a percentage of the measured kernel time).
+Without one, ``<label> Time (µs)`` and ``Pct <label>`` are left empty. An op
+projection that raises or returns anything else gets no columns for that
+op, with a one-time warning. Op projections are called once per op launch,
+so a slow one should cache its results.
+
+Roofline is always on; Origami for GEMMs and the SDPA tile model with Origami
+are built in behind flags. A proprietary library call belongs in an
+``--extension_file``, not in this repository.
+"""
+
+import numbers
+import warnings
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, Optional

+from . import origami_helper, sdpa_tile
+from .utils import add_duration_rate_columns, torch_dtype_map
+
+# Built-in labels come first in summaries, in this order; others follow in
+# column order.
+BUILTIN_LABEL_ORDER = ("Roofline", "Origami", "SDPA Tile Origami", "External")
+
+TIME_KEY = "time_us"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class OpWork:
+    """What an op does, independent of how long it took."""
+
+    category: Optional[str]
+    params: Optional[dict]
+    gflops: float
+    bytes_moved: Optional[float]
+    compute_spec: Optional[str]
+    bwd: bool = False
+    perf_model: Any = field(default=None, repr=False, compare=False)
+
+
+def get_compute_spec(perf_model):
+    """Compute spec (maf type + precision) of a perf model, such as
+    ``"matrix_fp16"`` or ``"vector_bf16"``, or None if not available."""
+    maf_type = (
+        perf_model.get_maf_type() if hasattr(perf_model, "get_maf_type") else None
+    )
+    precision = (
+        perf_model.get_compute_precision()
+        if hasattr(perf_model, "get_compute_precision")
+        else None
+    )
+    if maf_type is None or precision is None:
+        return None
+    return f"{maf_type}_{precision}"
+
+
+def op_work(perf_model, bwd=False):
+    """The :class:`OpWork` of a constructed perf model, forward or backward."""
+    gflops = (perf_model.flops() if not bwd else perf_model.flops_bwd()) / 1e9
+    bytes_moved = perf_model.bytes() if not bwd else perf_model.bytes_bwd()
+    params = getattr(perf_model, "param_details", None)
+    return OpWork(
+        category=getattr(perf_model, "bwd_category" if bwd else "category", None),
+        params=dict(params) if params is not None else None,
+        gflops=gflops,
+        bytes_moved=bytes_moved,
+        compute_spec=get_compute_spec(perf_model),
+        bwd=bwd,
+        perf_model=perf_model,
+    )
+
+
+def op_projection_columns(label):
+    """``(per-shape, per-instance)`` column names for an op-projection label.
+
+    Per-shape columns depend only on the op's params; per-instance columns
+    depend on the measured kernel time.
+    """
+    return (
+        [f"{label} Time (µs)", f"{label} TFLOPS/s", f"{label} TB/s"],
+        [f"Pct {label}"],
+    )
+

+def op_projection_labels(columns):
+    """Labels that have op-projection columns in ``columns``, built-ins first."""
+    columns = list(columns)
+    present = set(columns)
+    labels = [
+        col[len("Pct ") :]
+        for col in columns
+        if col.startswith("Pct ") and f"{col[len('Pct '):]} Time (µs)" in present
+    ]
+    rank = {label: i for i, label in enumerate(BUILTIN_LABEL_ORDER)}
+    return sorted(labels, key=lambda label: rank.get(label, len(rank)))
+
+
+def op_projection_group_columns(columns, label, labels):
+    """``label``'s columns, in column order, with ``Pct <label>`` included.
+
+    A column under a longer label that extends ``label`` (``"Origami X"`` vs
+    ``"Origami"``) belongs to that longer label.
+    """
+    longer = [other for other in labels if other.startswith(f"{label} ")]
+    return [
+        col
+        for col in columns
+        if col == f"Pct {label}"
+        or (
+            col.startswith(f"{label} ")
+            and not any(col.startswith(f"{other} ") for other in longer)
+        )
+    ]
+
+
+def _is_scalar(value):
+    return isinstance(value, (str, bool, numbers.Number))
+
+
+def add_op_projection_columns(
+    dict_metrics, label, output, gflops, bytes_moved, busy_kernel_time
+):
+    """Write ``label``'s columns for an op projection's ``output``: a dict with
+    an optional ``time_us`` and extra scalar columns."""
+    time_us = output.get(TIME_KEY)
+    extra_columns = {
+        name: value
+        for name, value in output.items()
+        if name != TIME_KEY and _is_scalar(value)
+    }
+    if not time_us and not extra_columns:
+        return
+    if time_us:
+        dict_metrics[f"{label} Time (µs)"] = time_us
+        add_duration_rate_columns(
+            dict_metrics, gflops, bytes_moved, time_us, prefix=label
+        )
+    else:
+        dict_metrics[f"{label} Time (µs)"] = float("nan")
+    for name, value in extra_columns.items():
+        dict_metrics[f"{label} {name}"] = value
+    dict_metrics[f"Pct {label}"] = (
+        (time_us / busy_kernel_time) * 100
+        if time_us and busy_kernel_time > 0
+        else float("nan")
+    )
+
+
+_op_projection_warnings = set()
+
+
+def _warn_op_projection_failed(label, work, error):
+    key = (label, work.category, type(error).__name__)
+    if key in _op_projection_warnings:
+        return
+    _op_projection_warnings.add(key)
+    warnings.warn(
+        f"Op projection {label!r} failed on a {work.category} op "
+        f"({type(error).__name__}: {error}); its columns are left empty for that "
+        "op. Shown once per op projection, category and error type.",
+        RuntimeWarning,
+    )
+
+
+def add_op_projection_outputs(
+    dict_metrics, op_projections, work, arch, busy_kernel_time
+):
+    """Run each ``{label: op_projection}`` on ``work`` and write its columns.
+
+    An op projection that raises or returns something other than a dict or
+    None gets no columns for this op; the others and the measured metrics are
+    unaffected."""
+    for label, op_projection in op_projections.items():
+        try:
+            output = op_projection(work, arch)
+            if output is not None and not isinstance(output, dict):
+                raise TypeError(
+                    f"returned {type(output).__name__}, expected a dict or None"
+                )
+        except Exception as error:
+            _warn_op_projection_failed(label, work, error)
+            continue
+        if output is None:
+            continue
+        add_op_projection_columns(
+            dict_metrics,
+            label,
+            output,
+            work.gflops,
+            work.bytes_moved,
+            busy_kernel_time,
+        )
+
+
+def compute_roofline_time_and_bound(gflops, bytes_moved, peak_tflops, mem_bw_gbps):
+    """Roofline-bounded time (µs) and bound type from FLOPs, bytes, and arch peaks.
+
+    The lower bound an op could achieve: whichever of compute time (flops /
+    peak TFLOPS) or memory time (bytes / peak bandwidth) is larger. Returns
+    ``(None, None)`` when any input is missing or there is no work to bound.
+
+    Args:
+        gflops: GFLOPs performed by the op.
+        bytes_moved: Bytes read + written by the op.
+        peak_tflops: Max achievable TFLOPS for the op's compute spec.
+        mem_bw_gbps: Peak HBM bandwidth in GB/s.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``(roofline_time_us, roofline_bound)`` where ``roofline_bound`` is
+        ``"COMPUTE_BOUND"`` or ``"MEMORY_BOUND"``.
+    """
+    if (
+        peak_tflops is None
+        or mem_bw_gbps is None
+        or bytes_moved is None
+        or not gflops
+        or gflops <= 0
+    ):
+        return None, None
+    # Compute time: flops / (peak_tflops * 1e12) gives seconds, convert to µs
+    compute_time_us = (gflops * 1e9 / (peak_tflops * 1e12)) * 1e6
+    # Memory time: bytes / (bandwidth_gbps * 1e9) gives seconds, convert to µs
+    memory_time_us = (bytes_moved / (mem_bw_gbps * 1e9)) * 1e6
+    roofline_bound = (
+        "COMPUTE_BOUND" if compute_time_us >= memory_time_us else "MEMORY_BOUND"
+    )
+    return max(compute_time_us, memory_time_us), roofline_bound
+
+
+def roofline_op_projection(work, arch):
+    """Roofline time: the larger of peak-compute time and peak-bandwidth time."""
+    if arch is None or work.compute_spec is None:
+        return None
+    maf_specs = arch.get("max_achievable_tflops")
+    peak_tflops = maf_specs.get(work.compute_spec) if maf_specs is not None else None
+    time_us, bound = compute_roofline_time_and_bound(
+        work.gflops, work.bytes_moved, peak_tflops, arch.get("mem_bw_gbps")
+    )
+    if time_us is None:
+        return None
+    return {TIME_KEY: time_us, "Bound": bound}
+
+
+def _time_output(time_us):
+    return None if time_us is None else {TIME_KEY: time_us}
+
+
+def origami_gemm_op_projection(work, arch):
+    """GEMM time from Origami."""
+    if work.category != "GEMM" or arch is None:
+        return None
+    params = work.params
+    dtype = params.get("simulation_dtype")
+    if dtype is None:
+        dtype = torch_dtype_map(params["dtype_A_B"][0])
+    return _time_output(
+        origami_helper.gemm_time_us(
+            arch, params["M"], params["N"], params["K"], params.get("B", 1), dtype
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def sdpa_tile_origami_op_projection(work, arch):
+    """TraceLens's attention tile model (``sdpa_tile.py``), with Origami
+    timing each tile GEMM. Origami only models GEMMs; the tiling is
+    TraceLens's own."""
+    return _time_output(
+        sdpa_tile.sdpa_tile_time_us(
+            work.perf_model, arch, origami_helper.gemm_time_us, bwd=work.bwd
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def default_op_projections(enable_origami_gemm=False, enable_origami_sdpa_tile=False):
+    """Built-in op projections, in report order: Roofline; Origami for GEMMs with
+    ``enable_origami_gemm``; the SDPA tile model with Origami with
+    ``enable_origami_sdpa_tile``."""
+    op_projections = {"Roofline": roofline_op_projection}

+    if enable_origami_sdpa_tile:
+        op_projections["SDPA Tile Origami"] = sdpa_tile_origami_op_projection
+    return op_projections

+"""SDPA tile model: attention split into one Q·Kᵀ and one P·V tile GEMM on
+one CU, scaled by the number of waves, plus softmax and memory terms.
+
+Any GEMM model can time the tiles. It's passed as
+``gemm_time(arch, M, N, K, B, dtype, force_to_l1, num_cus)``, for example
+:func:`TraceLens.PerfModel.origami_helper.gemm_time_us`. Without one there is
+no time.
+"""
+
+import math
+
+from .perf_model import SDPA, Softmax
+from .utils import name2bpe, torch_dtype_map
+
+
+def sdpa_tile_time_us(perf_model, arch, gemm_time, bwd=False):
+    """Tile-model time in µs for an SDPA perf model, or None for other ops."""
+    if not isinstance(perf_model, SDPA) or arch is None:
+        return None
+    params = perf_model.param_details
+    dtype_A_B = params["dtype_A_B"][0]
+    dtype = params.get("simulation_dtype")
+    if dtype is None:
+        dtype = torch_dtype_map(dtype_A_B)
+    name = type(perf_model).__name__
+    if bwd:
+        fa = name in ("flash_attention", "flash_attention_backward")
+        bytes = perf_model.bytes_bwd(name2bpe(dtype_A_B))
+        tile_time = sdpa_bwd_time_us
+    else:
+        fa = name == "flash_attention"
+        bytes = perf_model.bytes(name2bpe(dtype_A_B))
+        tile_time = sdpa_fwd_time_us
+    return tile_time(
+        arch,
+        dtype,
+        dtype_A_B,
+        bytes,
+        perf_model.B,
+        perf_model.H_Q,
+        perf_model.N_Q,
+        perf_model.N_KV,
+        perf_model.d_h,
+        fa,
+        gemm_time=gemm_time,
+    )
+
+
+def tile_gemm_time(arch, M, N, K, dtype, force_to_l1=False, gemm_time=None):
+    """Time in µs of one tile GEMM on one CU, or None without a GEMM model.
+
+    ``force_to_l1`` asks the model to treat the operands as cache resident,
+    as in flash attention."""
+    if gemm_time is None:
+        return None
+    return gemm_time(
+        arch,
+        M=M,
+        N=N,
+        K=K,
+        B=1,
+        dtype=dtype,
+        force_to_l1=force_to_l1,
+        num_cus=1,
+    )
+
+
+def sdpa_fwd_time_us(
+    arch,
+    dtype,
+    dtype_A_B,
+    bytes,
+    B,
+    H_Q,
+    N_Q,
+    N_KV,
+    d_h,
+    fa=True,
+    gemm_time=None,
+):
+    """Forward tile-model time in µs, or None without a GEMM model."""
+    force_to_l1 = False
+    block_N_Q = N_Q
+    block_N_KV = N_KV
+
+    if fa:
+        force_to_l1 = True
+        # Every Q tile block goes through full K and V, so we keep block_N_KV same
+        # and Q tile size is 128 for all the cases observed
+        block_N_Q = min(128, N_Q)
+        # block_N_KV = min(self.N_KV, self.N_KV)
+
+    num_blocks_N_Q = math.ceil(N_Q / block_N_Q)
+    # num_blocks_N_KV = math.ceil(N_KV / block_N_KV)
+    total_num_blocks = num_blocks_N_Q * B * H_Q
+    num_waves = math.ceil(total_num_blocks / arch["num_cus"])
+
+    qkt_time = tile_gemm_time(
+        arch,
+        block_N_Q,
+        block_N_KV,
+        d_h,
+        dtype,
+        force_to_l1,
+        gemm_time,
+    )
+    if qkt_time is None:
+        return None
+    qkt_time = num_waves * qkt_time
+
+    softmax_time = num_waves * Softmax.get_time(
+        arch,
+        block_N_Q,
+        block_N_KV,
+        name2bpe(dtype_A_B),
+        1,
+        force_to_l1=force_to_l1,
+        num_cus=1,
+    )
+    pv_time = tile_gemm_time(
+        arch,
+        block_N_Q,
+        d_h,
+        block_N_KV,
+        dtype,
+        force_to_l1,
+        gemm_time,
+    )
+    if pv_time is None:
+        return None
+    pv_time = num_waves * pv_time
+
+    mem_time = (
+        bytes
+        / N_Q
+        / N_KV
+        * block_N_Q
+        * block_N_KV
+        / (arch["mem_bw_gbps"] * 1000)
+        * num_waves
+    )
+    return qkt_time + softmax_time + pv_time + mem_time
+
+
+def sdpa_bwd_time_us(
+    arch,
+    dtype,
+    dtype_A_B,
+    bytes,
+    B,
+    H_Q,
+    N_Q,
+    N_KV,
+    d_h,
+    fa=True,
+    gemm_time=None,
+):
+    """Backward tile-model time in µs, or None without a GEMM model."""
+    force_to_l1 = False
+    block_N_Q = N_Q
+    block_N_KV = N_KV
+    qkt_time = 0
+    pv_time = 0
+
+    if fa:
+        force_to_l1 = True
+        # ∇Q is tiled — but it is not partitioned exclusively across thread blocks the same way ∇K and ∇V are.
+        # Instead, multiple thread blocks may contribute to the same ∇Q tile, which is why atomics are needed on ∇Q
+        block_N_Q = min(N_Q, N_Q)
+        block_N_KV = min(128, N_KV)
+
+    num_blocks_N_KV = math.ceil(N_KV / block_N_KV)
+    # Partition happens on ∇K and ∇V and not ∇Q
+    total_num_blocks = num_blocks_N_KV * B * H_Q
+    num_waves = math.ceil(total_num_blocks / arch["num_cus"])
+
+    qkt_fwd_time = tile_gemm_time(
+        arch,
+        block_N_Q,
+        block_N_KV,
+        d_h,
+        dtype,
+        force_to_l1,
+        gemm_time,
+    )
+    if qkt_fwd_time is None:
+        return None
+
+    qkt_fwd_time = num_waves * qkt_fwd_time
+
+    # B = B * H_Q, M = N_Q, N = d_H, K = N_KV
+    pv_fwd_time = tile_gemm_time(
+        arch,
+        block_N_Q,
+        d_h,
+        block_N_KV,
+        dtype,
+        force_to_l1,
+        gemm_time,
+    )
+    if pv_fwd_time is None:
+        return None
+    pv_fwd_time = num_waves * pv_fwd_time
+
+    if fa:
+        # In case of flash attention we have to recompute
+        # B = B * H_Q, M = N_Q, N = N_KV, K = d_H
+        qkt_time = qkt_fwd_time
+        pv_time = pv_fwd_time
+
+    # We don't need to model these GEMMs again,
+    # as we already have the times
+    p_grad_time = qkt_fwd_time
+    v_grad_time = pv_fwd_time
+    q_grad_time = pv_fwd_time
+    k_grad_time = pv_fwd_time
+
+    # p_grad_time = pv_fwd_time
+    # v_grad_time = qkt_fwd_time
+    # q_grad_time = qkt_fwd_time
+    # k_grad_time = qkt_fwd_time
+
+    softmax_time = num_waves * Softmax.get_time(
+        arch,
+        block_N_Q,
+        block_N_KV,
+        name2bpe(dtype_A_B),
+        1,
+        force_to_l1=force_to_l1,
+        num_cus=1,
+    )
+
+    # We assume that we use atomics for adding up the gradients together
+    atomic_latency_global_ns = 400  # ns for global memory
+    atomic_latency_local_ns = 40  # ns for shared memory/ L1
+    # This is the tile size for ∇K. For every tile of ∇Q, we need to accumulate the contributions
+    # from all the ∇K blocks
+    k_tile = block_N_KV
+    warp_size = 64
+
+    # Shared-memory tile reduction:
+    # Each block uses atomics only once per (k_tile × d)
+    # This optimization won't be there for now possibly?
+    num_k_tiles = math.ceil(block_N_KV / k_tile)
+
+    # Warp-level reduction:
+    # Each warp atomics once per d vector
+    # warps_per_block = (block_N_Q * self.d_h) // warp_size
+    warp_reduction_updates_per_block_global = math.ceil(
+        num_k_tiles * math.ceil(d_h / warp_size)
+    )
+    total_updates_global = warp_reduction_updates_per_block_global * num_waves
+
+    warp_reduction_updates_per_block_local = math.ceil(
+        k_tile * math.ceil(d_h / warp_size)
+    )
+    total_updates_local = warp_reduction_updates_per_block_local * num_waves
+
+    # Total atomic time (serialized across all blocks)
+    total_atomic_time_us = (
+        atomic_latency_global_ns * total_updates_global
+        + atomic_latency_local_ns * total_updates_local
+    ) / 1e3
+
+    # We have to read the first block and write the last block
+    mem_time = (
+        bytes
+        / N_Q
+        / N_KV
+        * block_N_Q
+        * block_N_KV
+        / (arch["mem_bw_gbps"] * 1000)
+        * num_waves
+    )
+    simulated_time = (
+        qkt_time
+        + pv_time
+        + p_grad_time
+        + v_grad_time
+        + q_grad_time

+### Add an op projection
+
+A *perf model* describes the work an op does: its parameters, FLOPs, and
+bytes. An *op projection* predicts how that work runs, usually as a time, and
+can report other per-op values, such as the kernel tile a library would pick.
+Each op projection has a label, and its columns appear next to the measured
+metrics and the roofline.
+
+An op projection is a function of the op's work and the GPU arch:
+
+```python
+def my_op_projection(work, arch):
+    ...
+    return None                                     # op not covered
+    return {"time_us": 12.5}                        # predicted time in µs
+    return {"time_us": 12.5, "Tile": "256x128x64"}  # time plus extra columns
+```

+The returned dict decides which columns the op gets. For an op projection
+labeled `MyModel`:
+
+| Return value | Columns added |
+| --- | --- |
+| `None` | None |
+| A dict with `time_us` | `MyModel Time (µs)`, `MyModel TFLOPS/s`, `MyModel TB/s`, `Pct MyModel` |
+| Any other dict key, such as `Tile` | `MyModel Tile` |
+
+`Pct MyModel` is the predicted time as a percentage of the measured kernel
+time. `time_us` is optional: a dict without it leaves the time columns empty
+and fills only its other keys. Only numbers, strings, and bools are written.

+The inputs are:
